entity.name: Sober Agentic Infrastructure, Inc.
entity.description: Sober Agentic Infrastructure, Inc. (SAI) is a Dallas, Texas company that builds and maintains VAREK, an open-source authorization runtime for autonomous AI agents released under the MIT license. SAI was founded in March 2026 by Kenneth Douglas, MD, a physician by training, on a clinical-reliability principle: medicine does not deploy systems that are usually right. VAREK applies that standard to AI agents that act with no human in the loop (HOOTL). Funding requested here supports work on the public VAREK repository: an independent security audit, maintainer time, and continued hardening of the runtime.

projects.name: VAREK
projects.description: VAREK decides whether each action an autonomous AI agent attempts is authorized, and enforces that decision at the operating-system kernel boundary. Policies are evaluated by an SMT decision procedure that returns one of three verdicts: SATISFIED, UNSATISFIED or UNKNOWN. Enforcement runs through the Warden, a default-deny supervisor built on seccomp-BPF and seccomp user-notify, which decides on the object actually delivered and so closes path-traversal, symlink and /proc/self escapes. Every ALLOW carries a proof object that an independent checker verifies in-line, and decisions are recorded in an unforgeable authorization log that can be exported as CycloneDX 1.6 evidence. VAREK runs on Linux, and on macOS through a Linux VM. Current release: v1.38.0. VAREK has not yet had an independent security audit; funding that audit is the first priority.
